intro: Gibraltar packs the Upper Rock, wild macaques and old fortifications into under 7 km², rewarding every slow walk with new views. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Gibraltar has no metro or tram. The local currency is the Gibraltar pound (£, GBP), not USD.
Citibus (routes 5 and 10) and Gibraltar Bus Company (other routes) run the buses. Single fares start at £1.00 to £1.80.
Bus fares are flat, so distance does not change the price. Gibraltar Bus needs exact change or card; Citibus takes cash only.
Taxis are the easiest way up the steep roads. Check locally for ride-app coverage, as Uber is not reliably available.
Driving is on the right. Much of the old centre has narrow, one-way streets and very limited parking, so park in La Línea and walk across the border.
Walking covers most of the town. A cable car links the town with the Upper Rock, and a cruise port sits at the western end of Waterport Road.

siege.name: Gibraltar Great Siege Tunnels
siege.price_text: Approx. USD 15–25 adult · check on the day
siege.hours: Usually daily, mid-morning to late afternoon · check on the day
siege.tip: Wear comfortable shoes and a light jacket, since the tunnels stay cool and damp inside.

moorish.name: Moorish Castle
moorish.price_text: Check on the day · usually included in Upper Rock access fees
moorish.tip: Walk the ramparts for views over the town and the bay. Expect uneven stone steps.

casemates.name: Main Street & Casemates Square
casemates.hours: Open at all times; shops and cafés follow their own hours
casemates.tip: Stop at the square for cafés and street life, then browse the shops on Main Street.

upper.name: Upper Rock Nature Reserve
upper.price_text: Approx. USD 25–45 entry · check on the day
upper.hours: Check on the day; the reserve is closed in bad weather
upper.tip: Book the cable car or a taxi tour early, and bring water since there is little shade.

cable.name: Gibraltar Cable Car
cable.price_text: Approx. USD 25–35 return · check on the day
cable.hours: Check on the day; times vary with weather
cable.tip: Ride up and walk down to see the Barbary macaques and the top viewpoints.

europa.name: Europa Point Lighthouse
europa.tip: Visit the lighthouse and mosque grounds, and look across the strait towards Africa.

catalan.name: Catalan Bay
catalan.hours: Open at all times; lifeguards in season only
catalan.tip: Head to the seafront cafés and fishing-village lanes for a relaxed local feel.

ocean.name: Ocean Village
ocean.price_text: Varies · dining costs depend on the venue
ocean.hours: Restaurants usually open for lunch and dinner · check on the day
ocean.tip: Book a waterfront table in advance for evenings, especially at weekends.

museum.name: Gibraltar Museum
museum.price_text: Approx. USD 5–15 · check on the day
museum.tip: Start here to get the Gibraltar history background before you visit the tunnels and castle.

stays.why: In the heart of the old town, steps from the Convent, Cathedral and Main Street shops. Best base for walking.
Quiet fishing village on the east side with a sandy beach and seafront bars. Taxi ride to the town centre.
Near the lighthouse, Europa Point mosque and Trafalgar Cemetery. Quieter, with sea views but fewer restaurants.
Marina hotels and restaurants close to the cruise port. Good for sunset walks and evening dining.

food: Try local Gibraltarian dishes such as calentita (chickpea flour cake) and rabo de toro (oxtail stew) in old-town restaurants.
Tapas bars along Main Street and Irish Town serve Spanish-style small plates. Share several to try more.
Fish and chips and pub meals are common near the marina and Ocean Village. Good for a relaxed dinner.
Bakeries and cafés in the old town sell cheap pastries and sandwiches for lunch on the go.
Many shops and cafés take card, but keep some small coins for buses. Prices are in pounds (£), so check menus before you order.
more_time: Spend a day in Spain: walk across the border from La Línea and take a local bus to nearby towns. Check bus times and border queues first.
Visit Gorham's Cave Complex on the Upper Rock, a UNESCO-listed Neanderthal site. Check opening days and tour times before you go.
Add a half-day for the Great Siege Tunnels and Trafalgar Cemetery. Both suit history fans and fit easily with a cable car trip.
